result.finding: Assessed 6 CWE rules in Concurrency & Synchronization: 0 FOUND, 6 NOT_FOUND
evidence: Full-repository source assessment, not a changed-code review. Reviewed all application Java, JavaScript, templates, runtime/deployment configuration and Oracle initialization scripts. Tests reviewed as corroboration, not counted as production vulnerabilities. Excluded generated target output, assessment outputs, skill instructions and .github/agents.

Static assessment only; no deployed application, native dependency internals, runtime exploitation or stress testing. NOT_FOUND denotes no confirmed application-source match, not a guarantee of security.

CWE-543: Spring-managed singleton controllers/services keep final injected dependencies and constructor-only configuration, not mutable per-request singleton state. Request lists/maps/results and ImageReader are method-local. Framework creates/publishes beans; no unsafe custom singleton construction found.

CWE-567: allowedMimeTypes is initialized once and never mutated; max size is final. Static fields are loggers/constants. Mutable maps/lists/entities are request/transaction local, with no shared cache or cross-thread writes found.

CWE-662: Persistence is mediated by Spring transactions and database concurrency; no application-managed exclusive mutable resource or unsynchronized cross-thread critical section identified. Concurrent deletes may produce not-found/errors but no demonstrated authorization/integrity bypass; no locks or optimistic @Version is not by itself a vulnerability.

CWE-667: No manual lock/unlock, synchronized blocks, semaphore, monitor wait/notify or lock-order logic. Database locking belongs to transactional persistence; no incorrect acquisition/release path in owned source.

CWE-820: Each upload constructs a distinct UUID entity and request-local state. There is no shared application-side mutable collection or read-modify-write counter that requires missing synchronization. Initialization scripts use check-then-create for deployment bootstrap; simultaneous invocation is not a demonstrated application attacker-controlled security violation.

CWE-821: Reviewed transaction boundaries, entity creation/deletion, injected singleton state and browser async upload flow; no synchronization primitive misuse, incorrectly selected monitor or incorrectly synchronized shared-state access found. No concurrency stress testing performed.

values.name: Use of Singleton Pattern Without Synchronization in a Multithreaded Context
values.description: The product uses the singleton pattern when creating a resource within a multithreaded environment.

values.name: Unsynchronized Access to Shared Data in a Multithreaded Context
values.description: The product does not properly synchronize shared data, such as static variables across threads, which can lead to undefined behavior and unpredictable data changes.

values.name: Improper Synchronization
values.description: The product utilizes multiple threads or processes to allow temporary access to a shared resource that can only be exclusive to one process at a time, but it does not properly synchronize these actions, which might cause simultaneous accesses of this resource by multiple threads or processes.

values.name: Improper Locking
values.description: The product does not properly acquire or release a lock on a resource, leading to unexpected resource state changes and behaviors.

values.name: Missing Synchronization
values.description: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner but does not attempt to synchronize access to the resource.

values.name: Incorrect Synchronization
values.description: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner, but it does not correctly synchronize access to the resource.
